Past customersOlder enquiriesOutstanding quotesRelevant reason + permission  Thoughtful follow-up

A thoughtful reason to get back in touch.

Reactivation starts with relevance and permission. It is an opportunity to restart a relationship, not a guaranteed sale.

  1. 01Choose eligible contacts
  2. 02Find a relevant reason
  3. 03Send an approved message
  4. 04Route responses to your team

Choose the right group

Use appropriate customer history, tags and activity to identify a suitable audience. Exclude opt-outs, invalid details and people who should not receive the message.

Make the reason useful

A return visit, a service update or a relevant offer should fit the relationship. AI can help prepare wording for review, not invent personal facts.

Keep replies connected

Bring supported responses back into the shared conversation and give interested customers a clear human next step.

Review what actually happened

Look at responses, opportunities and opt-outs. Adjust timing and content based on evidence, without assuming every quiet contact is ready to buy.

An illustrative event business

Remember the relationship.
Respect the timing.

Elena's events and catering business has past clients with different occasions and needs. A relevant follow-up begins with the relationship and the information she is allowed to use, then gives a person ownership of any reply.
